Note — nothing is patched into this module; every output follows the computer's own clock, in local time until the alt mode switch is flipped.
Calendar.notes: The trigger outputs are not 1ms pulses: calendar.cpp:132 sets 10V while the unit's progress is below 0.01, so the pulse is a hundredth of the unit and lasts from 10ms on the second to about three and a half days on the year. The stepped ramps use the subdivision table at calendar.cpp:25, {4, 60, 24, 7, 4, 12, 3, 12} for second through year; the readme's table lists 60 for the hour, 24 for the day, 7 for the week and 4 for the month, which is the code's list shifted by one row. The season ramp divides by a fixed 90 days (calendar.cpp:118) while summing the real lengths of the months elapsed, so a 92-day season passes 10V before it ends, and the year ramp divides by 365 days (calendar.cpp:121), so it passes 10V on the last day of a leap year. Local time is re-read once a second (calendar.cpp:85); UTC is re-read every sample.

Seed.notes: The unpatched seed is not random. seed.cpp:83 initialises currentSeed from a default-constructed std::mt19937, which has a fixed default seed, so every Seed module with an empty Seed jack produces the same sixteen voltages on every machine and at every launch; the readme says a random seed is used. The seed voltage is multiplied by 10000 and cast to unsigned int, so what a negative seed voltage does depends on the platform's float-to-unsigned conversion and was not tested here.

Note — drag the right-hand edge of the panel to make the module wider or narrower.

Spellbook.notes: Two things the readme does not match. In absolute index mode the row is (int)V modulo the row count (spellbook.cpp:663), which counts from zero, so 1V selects the second row rather than the first as the readme says; feeding the Absolute Index output back into the Index jack therefore lands one row late. And the Relative Index output divides by the row count minus one (spellbook.cpp:686), so a one-row sequence divides zero by zero and the jack carries a NaN. The sequence text is a custom text widget added with addChild, not a parameter, so it cannot be clicked for help; the same is true of the resize handles.
